subject: Performance / SLO qualification follow-up - context window & latency impact
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Singh <priyanka@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance / SLO qualification follow-up - context window & latency impact

Hi Priyanka -

Great to meet you and Steven today - thanks for the detailed walkthrough of FinCo's use case and constraints. Quick recap and next steps from our side on the performance / SLO items we discussed:

1) Targets and priority
- Primary SLO: 95th percentile response latency <= 200ms for short-chat (average input ~200 tokens, output ~80 tokens).
- Secondary: streaming/low-latency long-form for cases where outputs are 1k+ tokens - acceptable 95th up to 1.5s if streaming increments are under 250ms per chunk.
- Throughput: expected steady-state ~120 QPS for the primary chat route, bursts up to 300 QPS during market opens.
- Concurrency: typical per-customer concurrency ~40 concurrent streams.

2) Context window and token limits
- You mentioned document ingestion with up to 30k token contexts for retrieval-augmented generation. We discussed two modes:
  a) 32k context full prompt (client-side truncation) - higher latency impact and more KV cache pressure;
  b) Summarization/recall layer to reduce effective input size to ~8-12k tokens for latency-sensitive calls.

3) Observability & perf validation
- We'll run a perf test with sample prompts (attached example_prompts.jsonl) and provide a perf_test_plan.pdf with runner details and expected measurements: P50/P95/P99 latency, token/sec, GPU utilization, and streaming latency per chunk.

4) Next steps
- Action for FinCo: share a representative set of prompts and a few sample long-context documents (we can accept anonymized samples).
- Action for Redwood: schedule a dedicated perf run (we estimate 2-3 business days to execute and analyze), and propose a canary config if results are within targets.

Please confirm if the SLOs above map to your expectations and if you can share the sample prompt file today or tomorrow. Happy to jump on a short follow-up if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Performance / SLO qualification follow-up - context window & latency impact

Heads up on the perf side: a couple of engineering notes for the run -

- For 32k context runs we'll need to ensure model variant with extended KV cache is used; quantized variants change memory footprint but can slightly increase per-token latency (~5-12ms/token depending on kernel selection).
- Streaming behavior: we'll measure chunk sizes of 256 tokens (default) and 512 tokens to see latency tradeoffs; 256 token chunks typically keep per-chunk latency under 200-250ms on A100-80GB equivalent hardware with optimized kernels.
- Concurrency testing: we should emulate 40 concurrent sessions with realistic inter-message intervals (Poisson arrivals) to catch cache contention scenarios.

I attached the perf_test_plan.pdf and example_prompts.jsonl that Marissa referenced. I'll run initial tests as soon as FinCo shares representative prompts.

-rishi
Senior ML Engineer, Inference Performance
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
From: Priyanka Singh <priyanka@finco.com>

Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance / SLO qualification follow-up - context window & latency impact

Thanks Marissa and Rishi - this is helpful and matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from our engineering team:

- For the long-context RAG flows we can probably accept higher end-to-end latency for initial retrieval + generation (up to ~2s) as long as the UI shows streaming tokens quickly (first token <250ms).
- Our expected distribution: ~78% of calls are short-chat (<= 1k tokens total), ~18% are mid (1k-8k), and ~4% are long (8k-32k). Please bake that into the perf run.
- We'll share an anonymized set of 200 example prompts today (uploading to the Drive link), and a small set of full 20 long-context documents by end of day tomorrow.

Also, quick ask: can you include a run that shows impact of max_input_tokens set to 32k vs 12k so we can see comparative latency and cost delta?

- Priyanka

priyanka@finco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Performance / SLO qualification follow-up - context window & latency impact

Perfect - thanks for the prompt set, Priyanka. Confirming our plan and timeline:

1) Perf runs to execute (ETA 48 hours after we receive prompts):
- Baseline: short-chat profile (~200 input / 80 output tokens) at target concurrency to validate P95 <= 200ms.
- Mid: 1k-8k tokens profile to measure P95 and streaming behavior.
- Long: 8k-32k context runs comparing max_input_tokens=12k vs 32k (we'll report latency, token/sec, and estimated cost delta).

2) Deliverables
- Perf report (P50/P95/P99, GPU utilization, cost estimate, recommended quantization/profile)
- Canary configuration recommendation (instance types, autoscale thresholds, and fallback model variants)
- Recording of the run + raw logs (sanitized)

3) Next meeting: propose a 30-minute review on Mon 10 Aug 2026 10:00am PT - will you and Steven be available?

If anything changes on FinCo's side (sample sizes or SLA targets), let me know; otherwise we'll start the perf run as soon as we have the sample prompts in the Drive link you shared.

Thanks - looking forward to the results.
